mechanism: Exhaust adds fine particles to outdoor air.
strength_reason: Every source study read finds a substantial transport share, though the share varies widely by city, season and method (20% to 41% in three Delhi inventories; 32% to 57% in Jakarta). The World Bank's 2025 GAINS synthesis puts transport at 10-40% across IGP-HF jurisdictions (17% on average).
uncertainty: Shares differ by method and season; a city-wide share does not identify the main source at a particular hotspot.

mechanism: Construction and road dust add particles, mainly coarse ones.
strength_reason: Government and TERI-ARAI source studies attribute a large share of PM10, and a seasonal share of PM2.5, to dust.
uncertainty: Dust is a bigger share of coarse particles (PM10) than of fine particles, and more in summer than winter.

mechanism: Kiln smoke adds fine particles around kiln clusters during the firing season.
strength_reason: One modelling study attributes about 40% of measured fine particles north of Dhaka to kilns in the firing season; Bihar studies name kilns among main rural sources. The World Bank names small industry including kilns as a leading source in Nepal and Uttar Pradesh.
uncertainty: The Dhaka study was published in 2013; kiln technology has since changed in places.

mechanism: Industrial and power-plant emissions add particles and gases.
strength_reason: Source studies in Mumbai and Patna attribute 10% to 20% to industry; Singrauli shows high particulate levels near coal plants. The World Bank's synthesis puts industry and power at 21% of IGP-HF exposure on average, with small enterprises contributing more than heavy industry.
uncertainty: Inventories miss informal units, so industry shares from dispersion models may be too low.

mechanism: Smoke from household stoves escapes into outdoor air.
strength_reason: A national modelling study estimates household sources add enough to ambient PM2.5 that removing them would bring India's average to the standard; the World Bank states stoves create outdoor pollution. The World Bank's GAINS synthesis finds household cooking the only source in the top four in every IGP-HF jurisdiction modelled (33% on average, 2020-24).
uncertainty: Modelled estimate for a 2015 baseline; highly polluted areas such as Delhi would stay above the standard even without household emissions.

mechanism: Burning waste in the open adds smoke to local and city air.
strength_reason: Lahore's inventory attributes about 29% of PM2.5 emissions to waste burning; a Dhaka project is measuring landfill burning.
uncertainty: An emissions inventory share is not a measured concentration share.

mechanism: Crop-residue smoke travels across the region during the burning season.
strength_reason: Lahore averaged 175 µg/m³ on days its air had passed over active burning against 93 µg/m³ on other days.
uncertainty: Association by air-mass back-trajectory; other sources also rise in the same season.

mechanism: Gases react in the air to form nitrate, sulphate and ammonium particles.
strength_reason: Delhi source studies find secondary particles a major winter component of PM2.5.
uncertainty: Precursor gases come from many sources; this map does not assign secondary particles to a single sector.

mechanism: Low winds and a low mixing layer trap pollution near the ground.
strength_reason: TERI-ARAI attribute much higher winter concentrations to lower wind speed and boundary-layer height.
uncertainty: Weather changes concentrations without changing emissions, so a cleaner week is not proof that a policy worked.

mechanism: Pollution arriving from outside a city adds to its outdoor levels.
strength_reason: The World Bank finds PM2.5 at any South Asian location comes from sources over several hundred kilometres; Delhi's regional inflow varied between about a quarter and over a third in recent winters. On World Bank GAINS estimates, about half (52%) of PM2.5 in IGP-HF jurisdictions comes from outside local boundaries.
uncertainty: Regional share differs by city and year; it is not the dominant source everywhere.

mechanism: People in and beside traffic breathe exhaust before it mixes into city air.
strength_reason: Measurements inside Delhi auto-rickshaws found PM2.5 1.5 times, black carbon 3.6 times and ultrafine particles 8.4 times ambient, mostly from nearby vehicles.
uncertainty: Measured in auto-rickshaws and among delivery riders; other roadside occupations are not directly measured.

mechanism: Outdoor workers breathe outdoor air for long hours.
strength_reason: Delhi survey data show workplace exposure to outdoor air rises the lower a respondent's class; delivery riders measured high breathing-zone exposure.
uncertainty: Exposure itself was measured for few occupations; most evidence is self-reported time outdoors.

mechanism: Solid-fuel stoves fill homes with smoke.
strength_reason: Billions of people are exposed to household air pollution from solid fuels; in the HAPIN trial personal exposure without gas stoves was about three times that with them.
uncertainty: Exposure stays above the WHO guideline even with gas, because outdoor air and other sources remain.

mechanism: Outdoor pollution enters classrooms.
strength_reason: Classroom PM2.5 in Delhi was high enough for purifiers to reduce it significantly; infiltration from outdoors was not measured directly.
uncertainty: How much classroom air comes from outdoors was not reported in the sources read.

mechanism: Long- and short-term exposure raises death rates.
strength_reason: An Indian difference-in-differences study, a ten-city time-series study and GBD estimates all find higher mortality with higher PM2.5.
uncertainty: Death totals depend heavily on the comparison level chosen; more than fourfold difference between two standards.

mechanism: Long hours in polluted air at work are associated with damaged lungs.
strength_reason: Delhi waste pickers and sanitation workers had far more abnormal lung function than office workers, and Chennai vendors' lung function fell with years vending; but another Delhi study linked impairment to smoking and age rather than measured pollution.
uncertainty: Cross-sectional studies with small samples; smoking, dust and other workplace hazards are hard to separate from air pollution.

mechanism: Traffic fumes add to the burden on lungs of people who work in traffic.
strength_reason: High measured exposures among drivers and riders; respiratory outcomes for these groups were not measured in the sources read.
uncertainty: Exposure is measured; harm in this group is inferred from general evidence.

mechanism: Smoke during the burning season reduces lung function in nearby villages.
strength_reason: In six Patiala villages lung function fell during burning periods, by 16% in boys and 26% in girls aged 10 to 18.
uncertainty: One district study comparing seasons in the same people.

mechanism: Kitchen smoke harms the lungs of those who cook and of young children.
strength_reason: GBD attributes many deaths to household air pollution, but the HAPIN randomised trial found no clear effect on children's lung function even with near-complete gas use.
uncertainty: Observational associations and trial results point in different directions for some outcomes.

mechanism: Exposure during pregnancy is associated with lower birthweight.
strength_reason: A Tamil Nadu cohort found 4 g lower birthweight per 10 µg/m³, but the HAPIN trial found no significant birthweight difference when gas stoves cut exposure.
uncertainty: Association in a cohort; no effect in a randomised trial at the exposure reduction achieved.

mechanism: Outdoor fine particles during pregnancy are associated with preterm birth and low birthweight.
strength_reason: Two national survey analyses link higher in-utero PM2.5 to preterm birth and low birthweight.
uncertainty: Observational; satellite exposure estimates; effect on birthweight small in one analysis.

mechanism: Fine particles are associated with more respiratory infection and anaemia in children.
strength_reason: National survey data link each 10 µg/m³ to 11% more acute respiratory infection and 10% more anaemia.
uncertainty: Cross-sectional associations.

mechanism: Pollution shocks reduce hourly output at work.
strength_reason: In a Bengaluru garment factory hourly output fell with fine-particle pollution.
uncertainty: One formal-sector factory; transfer to informal work is uncertain.

mechanism: Illness raises spending on medical care.
strength_reason: Delhi households reported higher spending in pollution months, dominated by medical costs.
uncertainty: Self-reported spending; illness and spending were not linked person by person.

mechanism: Illness means missed work or slower work, and lost earnings.
strength_reason: No measured study of earnings lost to pollution-related illness among informal workers in India was found.
uncertainty: Plausible and important, but unmeasured.

mechanism: Medical bills and lost earnings push households into borrowing.
strength_reason: No study of pollution-related debt was found in the sources read.
uncertainty: Unmeasured.

mechanism: Severe air quality triggers emergency restrictions.
strength_reason: GRAP rules restrict construction as the index rises and ban it at Stage 4, and close primary classes at Stages III and IV.
uncertainty: Specific to Delhi-NCR's emergency plan.

mechanism: Construction bans and advisories stop daily earnings.
strength_reason: Court orders and compensation schemes exist because bans idle workers; women construction workers report losing earnings in peak months; work-from-home advisories do not reach daily-wage workers.
uncertainty: The size of the loss across all affected workers has not been measured.

mechanism: Unregistered workers receive no compensation for lost days.
strength_reason: Of about 1.38 million workers ever registered, only about 90,000 were active members in December 2024; in a site survey 5 of 75 workers were registered and none had been paid.
uncertainty: Dashboard figures and a small survey; registration rules change.

mechanism: Unspent welfare funds sit alongside low enrolment.
strength_reason: 44% of the national welfare cess was unspent; federations attribute low disbursement partly to weak enrolment.
uncertainty: National figures; the Delhi-specific link is not measured.

mechanism: Severe-pollution rules close primary classes.
strength_reason: Under GRAP Stages III and IV physical classes stop for children up to Class V, sometimes for up to 15 days with little notice.
uncertainty: Learning loss itself has not been measured.

mechanism: Construction bans are intended to cut dust during episodes.
strength_reason: The intended effect of GRAP construction bans on concentrations was not evaluated in the sources read.
uncertainty: Intended mechanism, not an evaluated result.

mechanism: Lost income leaves less to spend on protection such as masks, clean fuel or care.
strength_reason: Protective devices are concentrated among affluent households; whether lost wages reduce protection was not measured.
uncertainty: The ownership gap is measured; the effect of lost income on it is inferred.

mechanism: Those without means to protect themselves stay exposed.
strength_reason: Air conditioners and purifiers are owned mostly by the affluent; outdoor workplace exposure rises the lower the class; many waste pickers did not know of protective equipment.
uncertainty: Cross-sectional survey evidence.

mechanism: When gas refills cost too much, households go back to solid fuels.
strength_reason: In 2021-22 more than half of scheme beneficiaries bought four or fewer refills against about seven needed; research names refill cost, access and women's limited say in spending.
uncertainty: Refill counts are administrative; fuel stacking is common.

mechanism: Medical bills compete with fuel costs in household budgets.
strength_reason: No study linking pollution-related medical spending to clean-fuel purchases was found.
uncertainty: Unmeasured.

mechanism: Lost earnings leave fewer choices to avoid hazardous work.
strength_reason: No study of whether income loss keeps workers in more exposed jobs was found.
uncertainty: Unmeasured return link.

mechanism: Where there are no monitors, high exposure goes unrecorded.
strength_reason: About 40% of districts have no government monitor; Bihar has roughly one regulatory monitor per 3.5 to 4 million people, yet a 538-node sensor network found rural standards violated on most days.
uncertainty: Low-cost sensor data have their own accuracy limits.

mechanism: Unrecorded exposure is less likely to be prioritised.
strength_reason: Monitoring stations are only moderately correlated with pollution levels; whether this misdirects action was not measured.
uncertainty: Interpretation built on a measured mismatch.

mechanism: Places that are not prioritised get fewer new monitors.
strength_reason: No study of how monitor siting decisions respond to past data was found.
uncertainty: Unmeasured return link.

mechanism: Inventories that miss informal units understate their share.
strength_reason: In Mumbai receptor modelling gave industry 12% to 20% of PM while the inventory-based model gave under 1%, because small units were missing.
uncertainty: One city comparison; inventories are being revised.

mechanism: Polluting kilns face court orders and closure.
strength_reason: A Bangladesh High Court declared a kiln's operations illegal and ordered it shut; a Bihar notification required conversion to zigzag kilns.
uncertainty: Specific cases; enforcement is uneven.

mechanism: Conversion orders require owners to invest before savings arrive.
strength_reason: Zigzag conversion costs about Rs 40 lakh per kiln with a reported one- to two-year payback and needs trained workers. The World Bank's technology table gives zigzag conversions US$40,000-100,000 with 1.5-4 year paybacks.
uncertainty: Owner-reported payback; worker outcomes after conversion are unmeasured.

mechanism: Up-front cost and missing skills slow the switch away from high-emitting kilns.
strength_reason: A one- to two-year payback suggests cost alone may not block conversion; owners report trained workers as a constraint; most Bihar kilns reportedly converted after a mandate. The World Bank finds adoption limited despite attractive paybacks, citing upfront cost, finance, skills and weak enforcement.
uncertainty: Evidence points in different directions; the binding constraint varies.

mechanism: Debt-bound kiln workers live and work for months beside kilns.
strength_reason: Kiln workers live in temporary housing exposed to coal dust and heat for months; advances and withheld wages tie them to the season.
uncertainty: Exposure itself was not measured.

mechanism: Pollution that crosses borders cannot be solved by one city alone.
strength_reason: The World Bank concludes effective management requires coordination across sectors and upwind regions, and frames airsheds as extending beyond city and state boundaries.
uncertainty: A policy conclusion drawn from modelling.

mechanism: Without coordinated incentives across states, upwind burning continues.
strength_reason: No study linking coordination arrangements to burning levels was found; Punjab's recent decline was credited to machinery, enforcement and district plans.
uncertainty: Unmeasured; recent declines suggest state action can matter.

mechanism: Where alternatives to burning are costly or slow, farmers burn residue.
strength_reason: CAQM credits machinery, ex-situ straw use and enforcement for a 53% fall in fires; Thailand pays farmers for residue in a pilot.
uncertainty: Official attribution of a decline; not an evaluation.

mechanism: Uncompensated hardship may weaken compliance with emergency rules.
strength_reason: No study of compliance with GRAP or trust in it was found.
uncertainty: Interpretation only.

mechanism: Weaker compliance would let dust and other emissions continue during bans.
strength_reason: No compliance measurement was found.
uncertainty: Interpretation only.

mechanism: Waste pickers and residents burn waste and wood to keep warm, adding to their own exposure.
strength_reason: Nearly half of Delhi waste pickers surveyed burned wood or coal to keep warm and over 30% burned waste.
uncertainty: Self-reported behaviour; exposure not measured.

mechanism: Classroom pollution adds to children's exposure and symptoms.
strength_reason: An education campaign reduced self-reported breathing difficulty; purifiers lowered classroom PM2.5 but did not improve spirometry over education alone.
uncertainty: A trial of responses, not a direct measure of harm from classroom air.

mechanism: Sulphur dioxide from coal plants and industry forms sulphate particles in the air.
strength_reason: The World Bank names coal power plants' sulphur dioxide as a major source of secondary PM2.5 in the IGP-HF; secondary particles can make up 40-60% of PM2.5 mass.
uncertainty: Regional synthesis; shares of secondary PM by precursor are not given per jurisdiction.

mechanism: Ammonia from fertiliser and manure combines with other pollutants to form particles downwind.
strength_reason: The World Bank identifies agriculture as a major contributor to secondary PM2.5 through ammonia; Indian farm ammonia is described as forming particles downwind in Nepal's Terai.
uncertainty: Mechanism and modelled attribution; ammonia is not yet a regulated air pollutant in the region.

mechanism: Nitrogen oxides from traffic form nitrate particles in the air.
strength_reason: The World Bank lists nitrogen oxides from transport among the main precursors of secondary particles in the IGP-HF.
uncertainty: Regional synthesis.

mechanism: Particles that form in the air travel across city and national borders.
strength_reason: Precursor gases travel hundreds of kilometres before forming particles, making secondary PM a major cross-border issue in the World Bank's synthesis.
uncertainty: Mechanism; magnitude varies by season and place.
